story.title: Shooting at Seattle Food Festival Leaves Three Dead and Multiple Injured
story.summary: A shooting at a food festival in Seattle resulted in the deaths of three individuals, with four others injured, including a two-year-old boy. Authorities have indicated that the incident may be gang-related. One suspect is in custody, while another remains at large as investigations continue.

explore_lenses.label: Why do police now think there were three shooters?
explore_lenses.title: The initial two-person account has changed
explore_lenses.summary: Investigators now say the shooting may have involved at least three people and two opposing groups, not simply two people exchanging gunfire. That revision is based on evidence described in a juvenile-court filing and remains an active investigation.

claims.text: A juvenile-court document says investigators believe the 15-year-old in custody, a 19-year-old who died at the scene, and at least one unidentified person were shooters.
SPD Assistant Chief of Investigations Nicole Powell said investigators believe the violence may have been gang-related, with two groups firing at one another.
Police are reviewing video from buildings around the Seattle Center Armory, where the shooting occurred.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Police have not publicly identified the outstanding possible suspect or established a final motive; the gang-related assessment is preliminary.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the criminal case?
explore_lenses.title: A charging decision is the immediate next step
explore_lenses.summary: The detained suspect is a 15-year-old who has been ordered held in juvenile detention while investigators seek the other possible shooter and prosecutors assess the evidence. The public record so far describes an investigation, not final charges or findings of guilt.

claims.text: A judge ordered the 15-year-old held in juvenile detention on investigation of firearms violations and first-degree assault after he waived his initial appearance on July 27.
Forecast: the King County Prosecuting Attorney's Office said it expected Seattle police to refer the case on Wednesday, July 29, for a charging decision.
SPD has asked witnesses and people with video to contact its Violent Crimes Tip Line, indicating that public evidence gathering remains part of the investigation.

explore_lenses.label: What policy response are Seattle leaders seeking?
explore_lenses.title: Officials are advocating broader prevention measures
explore_lenses.summary: City councilmembers have framed the shooting as a reason to expand prevention and coordination, but their statements are proposals rather than announced city policy. Their approaches overlap on coordination while emphasizing different interventions.

claims.text: Public Safety Committee Chair Bob Kettle called for a comprehensive city public-safety effort and urged partnership from Mayor Katie Wilson's administration.
Councilmember Maritza Rivera urged the mayor to partner with the National Network for Safe Communities and said she intends to seek budget funding for that work.
Councilmember Eddie Lin called for sustained funding for community violence intervention, youth supports, safe storage, gun buybacks, red-flag laws, and universal background checks.

related_stories.title: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Stolen Unreleased Music and Content
related_stories.summary: Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against unidentified hackers who allegedly stole her unreleased music, photos, and videos. In her complaint, she claims that the breach has caused 'irreparable harm' to her career and is seeking a court order to compel internet providers to reveal the hackers' identities.

related_stories.title: Bryan Kohberger Seeks to Withdraw Guilty Plea in Idaho Student Murders
related_stories.summary: Bryan Kohberger, who pleaded guilty to the murders of four University of Idaho students in 2022, is now seeking to withdraw his guilty plea. This request follows his admission as part of a plea deal, and he is aiming to go to trial instead. Kohberger has filed a petition for post-conviction relief regarding his conviction.

related_stories.title: Trial Set for Singer D4vd in Murder of 14-Year-Old Celeste Rivas Hernandez
related_stories.summary: Singer D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, has been ordered to stand trial for the murder of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege that he dismembered her body, which was found in a Tesla registered to him. The trial follows a judge's ruling that sufficient evidence exists to proceed with the case.

related_stories.title: Gunfire Targets US Consulate in Toronto Again This Year
related_stories.summary: Shots were fired at the US consulate in Toronto, marking the second incident of this nature this year. Police engaged in a high-speed chase but did not apprehend the suspect, who remains at large. This follows a similar attack in June, which resulted in the arrest of three individuals.
